questions.question: Who composed Japji Sahib, the opening bani of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Japji Sahib is universally accepted as the composition of Guru Nanak Dev Ji and stands at the very beginning of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.

questions.question: How many pauris (stanzas) make up Japji Sahib, not counting its opening and closing saloks?
questions.explanation: Japji Sahib has 38 pauris, framed by an opening salok and a concluding salok.

questions.question: In which raag is Japji Sahib written?
options: It is not assigned to any raag
questions.explanation: Unlike almost all other compositions in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, Japji Sahib is not set to any raag; it is meant for recitation rather than singing.

questions.question: Asa Di Var is principally the composition of which Guru?
questions.explanation: Asa Di Var is by Guru Nanak Dev Ji: its pauris and most of its saloks are his, with some saloks by Guru Angad Dev Ji.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism – Asa ki Var

questions.question: How many verses does Jaap Sahib contain?
questions.explanation: Jaap Sahib by Guru Gobind Singh Ji consists of 199 verses praising the attributes and names of Akal Purakh.

questions.question: The Tav-Prasad Savaiye (Ten Savaiye) of the morning Nitnem are taken from which larger composition of Guru Gobind Singh Ji?
questions.explanation: The ten Tav-Prasad Savaiye form part of Akal Ustat, a composition of Guru Gobind Singh Ji in Sri Dasam Granth.

questions.question: According to the Sikh Rehat Maryada, which banis are recited in the morning Nitnem?
options: Rehras Sahib, Kirtan Sohila and Anand Sahib
Sukhmani Sahib, Asa Di Var and Japji Sahib
Japji Sahib, Sukhmani Sahib and Rehras Sahib
Japji Sahib, Jaap Sahib and the Ten Savaiye
questions.explanation: The Rehat Maryada prescribes Japji Sahib, Jaap Sahib and the Ten Savaiye (beginning 'Sravag sudh') in the morning, followed by Ardas.

questions.question: Rehras Sahib begins with a hymn from Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji whose opening word is:
questions.explanation: Per the Rehat Maryada, Sodar Rehras begins with nine hymns from Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, the first of which starts with 'So Dar'.

questions.question: When does the Sikh Rehat Maryada prescribe the recitation of Kirtan Sohila?
options: At night before going to bed
questions.explanation: Kirtan Sohila is the bedtime prayer; the Rehat Maryada says it is to be recited at night before going to sleep.

questions.question: How many shabads (hymns) make up Kirtan Sohila?
questions.explanation: Kirtan Sohila has five hymns: three by Guru Nanak Dev Ji, one by Guru Ram Das Ji and one by Guru Arjan Dev Ji.

questions.question: Which Guru composed Anand Sahib?
questions.explanation: Anand Sahib was composed by Guru Amar Das Ji in Raag Ramkali and is recited at the conclusion of congregational services.

questions.question: Anand Sahib has 40 pauris. How many are recited in its short form at the end of congregational services?
questions.explanation: The short form of Anand Sahib has six pauris: the first five and the last (40th), as stated in the Rehat Maryada.

questions.question: At what time is Asa Di Var traditionally sung in Sikh congregations?
questions.explanation: Asa Di Var, with its 24 pauris, is sung in the pre-dawn Raag Asa during the early morning service in Gurdwaras.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism – Asa ki Var

questions.question: The Barah Maha in Raag Majh in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji was composed by which Guru?
questions.explanation: Guru Arjan Dev Ji composed Barah Maha Majh (Angs 133-136). Guru Nanak Dev Ji's Barah Maha is a different composition, in Raag Tukhari.

questions.question: Which Guru composed Siddh Gosht ('discourse with the Siddhas')?
questions.explanation: Siddh Gosht is one of Guru Nanak Dev Ji's compositions in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, alongside Japji Sahib, Asa Di Var, Dakhni Oankar and Patti.
questions.source: Sikh Missionary Society UK – Guru Nanak Dev Ji
questions.note: Only authorship asked; raag and dialogue details not confirmed in an opened source.

questions.question: Who composed the 57 saloks (Salok Mahalla 9) that appear near the end of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji?
questions.explanation: Salok Mahalla 9 consists of 57 saloks by Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji and is recited at the conclusion (bhog) of a complete reading of Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji.
questions.note: Timing of composition is debated; only authorship asked.

questions.question: Which bani by Guru Arjan Dev Ji is the shortest of the 22 vars in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji, with only three pauris?
questions.explanation: Basant Ki Var by Guru Arjan Dev Ji has just three pauris and, unusually, no saloks attached, making it the shortest var in the Guru Granth Sahib.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism: Basant Ki Var

questions.question: The first hymn of Shabad Hazare (in Raag Majh) is traditionally understood as letters written by Guru Arjan Dev Ji to whom?
questions.explanation: Tradition holds that Guru Arjan Dev Ji wrote these verses as letters from Lahore to his father, Guru Ram Das Ji, expressing longing to see him.

questions.question: The opening stanza of the Ardas, invoking Akal Purakh and the first nine Gurus, is taken from which composition of Guru Gobind Singh Ji?
options: Var Sri Bhagauti Ji Ki (Chandi di Var)
questions.explanation: The Ardas begins with the prelude to Var Sri Bhagauti Ji Ki (also called Chandi di Var) by Guru Gobind Singh Ji.

questions.question: Benti Chaupai Sahib, also recited within Rehras Sahib, is a composition of which Guru found in which granth?
options: Guru Gobind Singh Ji, Sri Dasam Granth
Guru Arjan Dev Ji, Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji
Guru Hargobind Ji, Sri Dasam Granth
questions.explanation: Benti Chaupai was composed by Guru Gobind Singh Ji and is found in Sri Dasam Granth; the Rehat Maryada includes it in the evening Rehras.
